subject: Comment pitch: targeting climate finance where the exposure is
body:
Hi Megan,

I'm writing from Talaix (talaix.com), a climate-extreme intelligence platform built on satellite Earth observation and official open data — every finding source-labelled, no invented numbers.

A comment idea tied to two Climate Home News pieces from the past week: the Pacific Resilience Facility's first call for proposals, and the drought deal postponed to 2028. Both hinge on the same question — how do funders decide who is "most exposed"?

We can prepare an evidence-based analysis of exposure counts (population, hospitals, schools, infrastructure) for climate-vulnerable regions, with uncertainty stated.

I can send a 250-word pitch or a short brief first.

Best,
Motaz OMARIEN. Talaix

subject: Nepal's glacial flood — Earth-observation context on downstream exposure
body:
Hello,

I'm writing from Talaix (talaix.com), a climate-extreme intelligence platform working from satellite Earth observation, weather reanalysis and open data — all findings labelled by evidence class.

On the Nepal–Tibet flood: Al Jazeera and Reuters reported on 31 August that a glacier collapse triggered the deluge, with 903 people killed and thousands missing, and that a lake formed by the disaster is now overflowing into Nepal's rivers, raising the risk of new flooding.

Talaix can prepare satellite-based screening of the downstream area — terrain, flow paths, and what is exposed (settlements, hydropower, transport) — with source and resolution stated, not prediction.

We can provide a short brief or visuals if useful.

Best,

subject: Story tip — Mediterranean fire season through Earth-observation data
body:
Hi Erik,

Story tip from Talaix (talaix.com), a climate-extreme intelligence platform using satellite Earth observation and open data.

Two recent, source-labelled facts: wildfires in north-eastern Algeria have killed at least 12 people amid extreme heat and drought (Al Jazeera, 29 Aug); and Copernicus reported the hottest June–July on record for western Europe, with record-low soil moisture.

subject: Guest post idea — how to read satellite data for climate risk
body:
Hi,

I'm writing from Talaix (talaix.com), a climate-extreme intelligence platform that analyses wildfire, flood, drought, heat, wind and coastal hazards from satellite Earth observation and open data.

A guest-post idea: "How to read satellite data for climate risk" — a practical explainer on what indicators (FWI, soil moisture, sea-surface temperature) mean and how they should, and shouldn't, be used in reporting extremes. It could be anchored to Copernicus's July 2026 bulletin (record western-Europe heat; record July ocean surface temperatures).
